summary: PDF reader puts its invisible text exactly over the printed letters: each pdf.js text line is refitted in the PDF's own embedded font with the justification in the spaces, so selecting 'learning' no longer copies 't learning' and a double-click lands on the word under the pointer.

budget_impact.rationale: Presentation only: local text measurement on fonts pdf.js already loaded. No model call, network or stored data change.
budget_impact.before: text layer in a generic font, each line stretched evenly; 26-28% of its spaces over printed letters on the test paper
budget_impact.after: text layer in the embedded font, justification in the spaces; 0-2.2% of spaces over printed letters on all 18 pages

open_risks: Measured in Chromium (preview pane), not in WebKit (the macOS app engine); a real double-click could not be simulated there.
Checked on one real paper (Nimbus Roman, IEEE two-column); papers in Computer Modern or with re-encoded fonts were not measured. Lines that cannot be fitted safely keep the pdf.js layout.
